sections.heading: The quarter
sections.text: Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) generated about $18.63 billion under DFB’s cash-capex free-cash-flow calculation in its fiscal 2027 first quarter, ended September 30, 2026—down about 27% from a year earlier. DFB defines this measure as operating cash flow minus cash additions to property and equipment. The comparison uses reported figures before rounding for presentation.

sections.heading: Dividends and other cash uses
sections.text: Cash dividends paid were about $6.76 billion, or roughly 36% of that measure. This comparison does not account for every competing use of cash: the amount left after dividends is not necessarily available for discretionary spending.

sections.heading: Finance leases
sections.text: Finance-lease principal also sits outside this cash-capex measure. Microsoft separately reported $1.0 billion of financing cash outflows from finance leases. Deducting that principal would produce a different analytical measure; lease interest already included in operating cash flow should not be deducted again.

sections.heading: The next comparison
sections.text: The next quarter will provide another comparison. For now, these figures describe one period—not a forecast of future dividends. Keeping cash capital spending, lease principal and distributions separate makes the change easier to interpret.

briefs.limitations: Cash-capex free cash flow is DFB-defined operating cash flow less cash additions to property and equipment, not an issuer-reported FCF figure. The additional lease-principal deduction is analytical. Derived figures are arithmetic on rounded reported inputs; the dividend remainder excludes other investing and financing cash flows. One quarter does not establish future distribution capacity.

sections.heading: Cash generation
sections.text: Keurig Dr Pepper’s November 3 earnings release details cash generation alongside substantial financing obligations. For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow was $2.220 billion. Subtracting $457 million of property, plant and equipment purchases and adding $145 million of disposal proceeds produces KDP’s reported non-GAAP free cash flow of $1.908 billion.

sections.heading: Other financing claims
sections.text: Common cash dividends of $938 million leave a calculated $970 million difference against that free-cash-flow measure. This is before other financing uses, including $107 million of preferred dividends, $64 million of distributions to non-controlling interests and $146 million of finance-lease payments. Excluding property-disposal proceeds, operating cash flow less PP&E purchases was $1.763 billion; this is a separate calculation, not KDP’s defined free cash flow.

sections.heading: Current obligations
sections.text: At September 30, KDP reported $1.290 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $7.270 billion of short-term borrowings and the current portion of long-term obligations. That balance-sheet classification alone does not establish individual repayment dates.

sections.heading: What remains
sections.text: The near-term question is how much cash remains after distributions and other commitments as the company works toward its planned separation. The release supports a cash-coverage observation, not a dividend-safety guarantee.

briefs.limitations: Issuer-defined non-GAAP free cash flow includes PP&E disposal proceeds. The common-dividend difference is not unrestricted or discretionary cash and excludes other investing and financing uses. Operating cash flow less PP&E purchases is a separate analytical measure. Balance-sheet current classification alone is not an individual repayment schedule. Historical cash coverage is not a guarantee or forecast of dividends. The release financial statements are unaudited. Exhibit 99.1 is furnished under Item 2.02, not deemed filed for Section 18; issuer and SEC copies are two official representations of the same company statement, not independent economic corroboration.

sections.heading: Charge and cash
sections.text: 3M’s November 4 filing separates a $7.35 billion nominal settlement commitment from a planned pretax charge of approximately $5.8 billion. The charge, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, reflects the present value of contributions under its November 3 PFAS personal-injury settlement, rather than an immediate cash payment.

sections.heading: Payment timing
sections.text: An initial $50 million is due within 30 days of the settlement. No payments are scheduled in 2027. The first $1.045 billion main installment is scheduled for January 15, 2028, or 30 days after termination rights are exhausted or waived, whichever is later.

sections.heading: Conditional schedule
sections.text: The six main installments add to $6.27 billion. Including the initial payment and potential additional payments, the schedule’s listed maximum totals $7.35 billion through 2034. Actual amounts and timing depend on participation and other conditions; all payments after the initial one are contingent on neither party exercising termination rights.

sections.heading: What remains
sections.text: 3M says the charge will be treated as a special item in adjusted results and leaves its 2026 guidance unchanged. That accounting treatment does not remove future cash obligations. The question to follow is how settlement participation and conditions translate into actual payments alongside the company’s other commitments.

briefs.limitations: This record describes settlement terms as of November 3, 2026, not a historical operating reporting period. Contractual payment dates extend into the future; the reported charge is approximate present value, not an immediate cash outflow. The schedule lists maximum amounts, with participation, termination and other conditions. The filing was dated November 3 but the SEC index gives a November 4 filing date; no exact public-availability timestamp is claimed. No estimate of dividend coverage or dividend safety is made. The issuer release and SEC filing are official company representations, not independent economic corroboration.

sections.heading: Quarterly shareholder cash returns
sections.text: ConocoPhillips distributed $3.408 billion through dividends and share repurchases in the third quarter, against $4.039 billion of company-defined free cash flow, according to its November 5 earnings materials. That left a calculated $631 million before other cash uses, rather than a measure of the quarter’s change in cash.

sections.heading: The issuer cash-flow definition
sections.text: The non-GAAP measure starts with $7.195 billion of operating cash flow, removes a $23 million working-capital contribution and deducts $3.133 billion of capital expenditures and investments. Dividends paid were $1.007 billion, with repurchases accounting for the remaining $2.401 billion distributed.

sections.heading: Separate asset-sale proceeds
sections.text: Asset sales brought in a separate $1.566 billion. Those proceeds sit outside the free-cash-flow measure and should not be treated as recurring operating cash. Other investment flows, financing payments and exchange-rate effects also mean the $631 million residual is not the actual cash-balance movement.

sections.heading: The next dividend period
sections.text: The company also raised its quarterly ordinary dividend to $0.93 per share, effective for the fourth-quarter payment due December 1. That future rate is separate from the third-quarter cash already paid. Whether operating cash generation can sustain dividends, investment and buybacks remains a question for subsequent periods.

limitations: All cash-flow inputs are quarterly USD millions for July 1 to September 30, 2026; the announcement event and new dividend observation date are November 5.

CFO and FCF are issuer-defined non-GAAP measures, not GAAP operating cash or necessarily comparable with similarly named measures elsewhere. CFO removes the positive 23 million operating working-capital effect.

The 631 million arithmetic residual is neither the actual 1252 million change in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash nor a claim of unrestricted, discretionary cash. Other investing and financing flows and exchange-rate effects remain separate.
Asset-disposition proceeds of 1566 million are the quarterly cash-flow line, outside the issuer FCF measure; no transaction-value or recurring operating-cash claim is made.

The 0.93 dividend is the newly announced fourth-quarter rate, payable December 1, 2026, to holders of record November 16. It is not the rate used to derive third-quarter dividends paid; no annualization or future share-count assumption is made.

Issuer and SEC copies of the same company material are representation cross-checks, not independent economic corroboration. This historical cash-flow comparison is not a dividend forecast, investment recommendation or safety guarantee.

sections.heading: Completed new issue
sections.text: Apple completed a $7.5 billion debt issue on November 9, selling seven series of senior unsecured notes. Of that principal, $3.25 billion matures in 2028 and 2029, about 43% of the new borrowing. The remaining maturities extend through 2036, according to its new SEC filing.

sections.heading: Rate structure
sections.text: The issue combines $6.25 billion of fixed-rate notes, with annual coupons ranging from 4.65% to 5.35%, and $1.25 billion of floating-rate notes. The floating rates reset quarterly using compounded SOFR plus contractual spreads. These are the terms of this issue, not Apple’s entire debt portfolio.

sections.heading: Two separate exposures
sections.text: The structure separates interest-rate exposure from repayment timing. Fixed coupons keep the stated interest rate unchanged, but the principal still comes due on schedule. Floating coupons leave interest payments exposed to changes in the reference rate. Neither feature establishes how Apple will fund the eventual repayments.

sections.heading: Actual use remains unspecified
sections.text: Apple’s prospectus estimated approximately $7.47 billion of net proceeds after underwriting discounts and expenses. It lists buybacks and dividends among several possible corporate uses, alongside investment and debt repayment. How much ultimately goes to each purpose remains unspecified; the borrowing alone does not demonstrate that dividends require debt funding.

limitations: November 9 is actual completed issuance and SEC filing date. November 5 is the underwriting agreement date and earliest event on the cover; it is not presented as the completion date. The prospectus was dated November 5 and filed November 6.
The reporting period is the point-in-time November 9 issuance, not an accounting quarter. The estimated net proceeds are a separately declared November 5 offering estimate.
All principal figures are face amounts of this new issue only, not net proceeds or total Apple debt. The $3.25 billion figure adds four series maturing November 9, 2028 and November 9, 2029.
The calculated 43 percent is 3250/7500*100 rounded to the nearest whole percent. Remaining principal matures in 2031, 2033 and 2036.

Fixed coupons are not yield to maturity or an assertion of Apple’s effective post-hedge financing costs. Floating rates reset quarterly based on compounded SOFR plus contractual spreads. No total interest-expense forecast is made.

The $7.47 billion net-proceeds figure is an approximate issuer estimate, not confirmed final realized proceeds. Permitted general corporate uses do not establish actual allocation or a need to borrow to pay dividends.

Both primary documents are issuer-authored SEC filings. No separate bond press release was found on Apple investor relations; the actual final prospectus supplement is the issuer supplement, accurately labeled as SEC-hosted. No recommendation, valuation conclusion or safety guarantee is made.

sections.heading: New board decisions
sections.text: TSMC’s board approved approximately US$40.93 billion in capital appropriations on November 10, alongside a NT$9-per-common-share dividend for the third quarter of 2026. The decisions put shareholder distributions and substantial investment plans on the same agenda.

sections.heading: Dividend and earnings
sections.text: The dividend equals about 31% of the quarter’s NT$29.43 diluted earnings per share, an earnings comparison rather than cash-flow coverage. Common shareholders have a March 11, 2027 ex-dividend date, a March 17 record date and an April 8 payment date. The NT$9 figure is not a per-ADS amount.

sections.heading: Capital scope
sections.text: The capital authorization covers manufacturing and packaging capacity, fab construction and facility systems, plus 2027 research-and-development investment, sustaining expenditures and capitalized leased assets. Appropriations authorize projects; they do not establish that US$40.93 billion has already been spent or that the entire amount belongs to one year’s cash-capex budget.

sections.heading: Investment timing
sections.text: Separately, directors approved up to US$500 million for Anthropic common shares at its initial-public-offering price and up to US$500 million for OpenAI preferred stock. These are investment ceilings, not disclosed completed purchases. The filing leaves the timing of these cash outlays, and their interaction with future operating cash generation, unresolved.

briefs.limitations: Board appropriations and investment ceilings are not realized cash expenditures, annual capex guidance or a financing commitment. Dividend/EPS uses rounded per-common-share figures for Q3, not cash-flow coverage, an ADS dividend or an annualized distribution.
